assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a NEW production building sprite: a LOW SQUARE INTERACTIVE TRADING TABLE for a RimWorld-like spaceship game, not a standing computer. The attached cargo-port image is ONLY a reference for gray metal palette, clipped corners, dark outline weight and broad panel detailing. DO NOT reproduce the upright monitor or the cargo hatch.
CRITICAL CAMERA CONTRACT: true orthographic PLAN VIEW, camera exactly 90 degrees above a HORIZONTAL tabletop. We see only horizontal top surfaces. All four outer edges have the SAME very narrow thickness treatment. No visible front wall, legs, feet, plinth front, upright screen, tilted monitor, rising back, perspective taper, isometric view, or cast shadow. The sprite will be rotated freely through 360 degrees as a flat game texture; it must never appear to be a sideways or upside-down standing cabinet.
Object: one compact 1x1 clipped-square industrial interaction table, centered on a square canvas, outer silhouette about 88 percent width and height, equal transparent margin. Strong dark perimeter, medium neutral-gray flat top divided into a few clear functional zones. A central horizontal inset dark-teal glass screen occupies about one third of the tabletop area (roughly 58% width by 55% height). Screen shows a simple network of 4 cyan square cargo nodes connected by broad thin right-angle lines, plus one small grouped pair of data blocks; no arrows, writing or directional page layout. Along the LEFT part of the table are three broad dark recessed input pads with a light gray inset center and one small circular control seen from directly overhead. Along the RIGHT part is an integrated short rectangular communications/data module, a pair of cable sockets and ONE short stout U-shaped conduit, all viewed from overhead and contained within the square. A modest three-slot vent and two tiny teal/amber indicator tiles occupy the remaining rim, with a few purposeful wide panel seams. Functional asymmetry without a vertical 'face'. Not a floor tile or empty hatch: distinct glass touch surface and tangible input/interface modules make it a working desk.
Style matches the cargo reference: clean dark outlines, muted gray industrial plates, restrained cyan accents, 2-3 broad shaded planes per component, medium-low detail designed to read at 48 pixels per tile. No microscopic screws, dense text, greeble noise, bright halo, glossy reflections, photoreal rendering, scenery, floor tile, pawn, UI frame or background. Genuinely transparent background including corners. Produce one sprite only.

Use case: stylized-concept. Generate one single game UI command icon for SEALED CARGO mode, transparent background, square 1024x1024 canvas. A centered blue-gray sealed shipping crate, simple slightly elevated three-quarter icon view, broad closed solid blue lid with visible seam, neutral gray front, chunky almost-black outlines, a narrow pale edge highlight, only two or three broad shading levels. No padlock: sealed is NOT locked. No arrows, no text, no check mark, no border or UI button background, no ground shadow, no glow. RimWorld command icon simplicity, crisp flat illustrated silhouette instantly legible at 48px. Fill central 82% of canvas. This will be paired with an open green crate icon for active storage. Exactly one object. Genuinely transparent empty margins.

revisions.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE production RimWorld-like top-down building sprite on a genuinely transparent background, square 1024x1024 canvas. Reference image 1 is our approved cargo loading port: use specifically its TOP LEFT UPRIGHT TERMINAL as the design-language reference, not the entire cargo port. Reference image 2 is the old station trade terminal to replace; do not retain its flat panel appearance or yellow corner decorations. Reference image 3 is the vanilla ancient terminal, reference for a standing machine silhouette only.
Subject: a standalone 1x1 station trading terminal, from the same manufacturer as the enlarged terminal in reference 1. Broad squat standing gray cabinet, large cyan-blue display occupying most of the upper cabinet, short projecting operator shelf on the south/bottom edge, two solid feet framing a dark recessed lower panel. A simple pair of opposing pale arrows on the cyan screen suggests trade. Strong dark outlines, clipped corners, neutral gray plates, just two or three broad shading values per surface. Match the approved cargo terminal's scale of details and gray tone. Orthographic game sprite looking down with the same slight front-face visibility as that terminal, no isometric rotation. Front/operator edge is at bottom. Center the cabinet horizontally and vertically, occupy about 90% of canvas width and 88% height; keep all outlines inside canvas. Transparent empty background including corners. No floor plate, cargo hatch, socket, accessories, ground shadow, glow halo, text, numerals, yellow hazard stripes, micro detail, photoreal reflections, extra screens or buttons. This must read clearly at 48x48 pixels.
revisions.reason: Superseded: giant trade symbol and empty control shelf were too simplistic.

revisions.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Rework reference image 1, our station trade terminal building sprite, which is TOO SIMPLISTIC and looks like a giant UI icon. Reference image 2 is our approved cargo port: its upper-left standing terminal supplies the family silhouette, dark outline weight and neutral-gray metal palette. Reference image 3 is a vanilla RimWorld Odyssey console: use only as a reference for believable functional machinery detail density, not as a source to copy.
Deliver ONE isolated 1x1 upright station trade computer sprite, square transparent canvas. Keep the centered clipped-corner gray cabinet, dark feet, front-facing operator edge at bottom, same orthographic top-down game viewpoint and footprint as image 1. Give it MEDIUM detail, still clean and readable at 48px:
- Rebalance the cabinet so the blue-cyan main screen occupies about the upper-central 35 percent of the machine rather than almost the entire face. Narrow the many nested screen bevels.
- On the screen, two compact pale opposing trade arrows and two or three short broad ledger rows; no letters/numbers. Darker desaturated teal background with restrained bright cyan shapes, no bloom.
- A real projecting south-side control deck occupying the lower central quarter: recessed dark keyboard with two rows of broad key groups and one wide spacebar, one distinct round control at the right. Strong clear shelf outline.
- A narrow right-side integrated interface bay with a short horizontal card/data slot, two small status lights and a stout cable connector. A simple three-slot vent on the opposite side. These are legible mechanical blocks, not filigree.
- Show a modest raised rear equipment cap and a recessed lower access panel between the feet, with a few purposeful panel seams. No busy armored frame.
Palette neutral gray casing, dark recesses, teal/cyan screen, tiny muted amber status light. Flat RimWorld illustration, hard black/dark gray contours, two or three broad value planes per part, slightly worn industrial hardware without scratches/noise texture. Avoid turning it into photoreal 3D or a glossy toy. No huge central symbol, no signboard appearance, no floor tile, no pedestal outside the footprint, no antenna, extra objects, cargo hatch, perspective/isometric rotation, ground shadow, external glow, tiny screws or dense key lettering. Preserve genuinely transparent background and transparent corners. Center body and keep all edges inside canvas with roughly 6-8 percent transparent margin.
revisions.reason: Superseded: upright front view does not remain plausible under free spaceship rotation.
